rfm_tuples.R: Recent public disclosures relating to MSG Networks have indicated that MSG Networks management can provide no assurance that it will be able to refinance its credit facilities prior to the maturity thereof in October 2024 and that, if a refinancing is not completed, MSG Networks would decide to enter into a work-out or seek bankruptcy protection prior to the lenders exercising their rights under the MSG Networks credit facilities.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B counterparty disclosure mirror. MSGS attributes the distress to MSG Networks's own filings without acknowledging MSGS's first-order exposure. Pull the corresponding language from Sphere Entertainment (MSG Networks' parent, CIK 0001795250) 10-K (same Aug 2024 filing window) and 10-Qs via edgar_fts to test whether the counterparty discloses substantial doubt explicitly.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Sphere Entertainment 10-K filed 2024-08-14 (one day after MSGS 10-K) states explicitly: 'the conditions with respect to the MSG Networks Credit Facilities raise substantial doubt about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern' — auditor flagged it as a Critical Audit Matter on whether substantial doubt was 'effectively alleviated.' Sphere repeated 'substantial doubt' language in 10-Qs filed 2024-02-05, 2024-05-10, 2024-11-12, and 2025-05-08 (5 hits). MSGS 10-K uses only softer 'no assurance' wording and never says 'going concern' or 'substantial doubt' about MSG Networks.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest investors who read both filings learn MSG Networks is in formal substantial-doubt status; MSGS 10-K downplays this by quoting MSG Networks's own conditional language. MSGS depends on MSG Networks for 17% of revenue and 50% of receivables — material euphemism.

rfm_tuples.R: Revenues from MSG Networks amounted to $175,325, $172,340 and $163,037 for the years ended June 30, 2024, 2023 and 2022, which represented 17%, 19% and 20%, respectively, of the Company's consolidated revenues... Entity A 50%, Entity B 16%, Entity C 18% of consolidated receivables balances [June 30, 2024].
rfm_tuples.f: Customer concentration claim — quantify the joint exposure to MSG Networks (the obligor counterparty in substantial-doubt status). Compare receivables concentration vs. revenue concentration to flag whether AR is unusually back-loaded for the distressed counterparty.
rfm_tuples.M_value: MSG Networks is Entity A: 50% of receivables but only 13% of consolidated revenue. This means MSG Networks owes MSGS a disproportionately large share of outstanding receivables relative to current-year revenue — i.e., MSGS is carrying expanded credit exposure precisely as the counterparty's solvency deteriorates. Add Sphere's other affiliate (likely Entity B at 16%, related-party local-media stack) and 66% of receivables are exposed to one financially distressed corporate complex.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: 10-K does not connect Entity A=50% AR with MSG Networks substantial-doubt status. A reasonable reader would expect either an AR write-down reserve, factoring, or escrow disclosure — none exists. The receivable build during distress is a Mode B forensic flag.

rfm_tuples.R: All borrowings under the Knicks Revolving Credit Facility and the Rangers Revolving Credit Facility are subject to the satisfaction of certain conditions, including representations as to the absence of a bankruptcy event... The Rangers Credit Agreement includes an event of default that is implicated by a bankruptcy event with respect to a material media rights counterparty, including MSG Networks.
rfm_tuples.f: Covenant / cross-default verification. Confirm magnitude: as of June 30, 2024, Knicks Revolving Credit Facility is fully drawn ($275M / $275M); Rangers is undrawn but the credit agreement contains a media-rights cross-default. Map to Sphere TSA event in subsequent 10-Q.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Knicks revolver is MAXED at $275M draw against $275M ceiling. Rangers revolver undrawn but Rangers facility cross-defaults on MSG Networks bankruptcy. Subsequent 10-Q (filed 2025-05-02, pre-cutoff) discloses on 2025-04-24 the Teams entered a Transaction Support Agreement with MSG Networks/Sphere consenting to a 28% Knicks media-rights-fee cut and 18% Rangers cut, elimination of escalators, contract shortened by ~6 seasons to 2028-29, in exchange for penny warrants for 19.9% of MSG Networks equity — i.e., MSGS effectively accepted a forced concession to forestall a bankruptcy event that would have tripped the Rangers cross-default and frozen Knicks/Rangers liquidity.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The 10-K (Aug 2024) downplays the cross-default risk by burying it in risk factors. By the 2025 Q3 10-Q the cross-default risk had already crystallized into a material giveback of contractually-protected media revenue. Stated annual local media rights fees fall to $162,939 (FY25) and $139,237 (FY26) vs. $186,700 originally stated — ~25% revenue impairment on the single largest contracted cash stream.

rfm_tuples.R: We believe we have sufficient liquidity, including approximately $89,136 in Cash and cash equivalents as of June 30, 2024, along with $250,000 of additional available borrowing capacity under existing credit facilities, to fund our operations and satisfy any obligations, for the foreseeable future. If MSG Networks were to experience a bankruptcy event, we would be prevented, absent a cure or waiver, from borrowing additional amounts under our revolving credit facilities.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B liquidity stress test. The stated $250M of additional capacity is the undrawn Rangers facility — which is precisely the one that would be unavailable upon an MSG Networks bankruptcy event (per the same paragraph). So the 'sufficient liquidity' assertion is conditional on the very risk the disclosure is hedging against.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Net true unconditional liquidity = $89,136 cash + $0 unconditional revolver capacity (Knicks fully drawn; Rangers conditioned on MSG Networks solvency). Knicks revolver at 6.69% variable interest; total long-term debt $275M + $30M NHL advance = $305M, of which $30M is payable on NHL demand. The disclosed 'foreseeable future' assertion materially overstates available liquidity to a reasonable reader who does not stitch the two sentences together.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Standard sports-credit-facility behavior, but the framing pairs a confident liquidity sufficiency claim with a contingent backstop that fails exactly when needed. Cash flow from ops also FELL from $152M to $92M YoY (-40%) despite higher operating income — a sign of working-capital strain (related-party receivable build) consistent with C2.

rfm_tuples.R: Based on the current roster the Knicks would be a luxury tax payer for the 2024-25 season... If we are required to pay the NBA a luxury tax, we would also no longer receive luxury tax proceeds as a non-tax paying team.
rfm_tuples.f: Cost step-up confirmation. Quantify the two-sided expense swing: (a) outflow as a luxury-tax payer, plus (b) loss of the prior allocated luxury-tax receipts. Pull FY24 baseline from MD&A.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY24 net provisions for league revenue sharing & NBA luxury tax = $44.3M (a credit-net position because Knicks were NOT a tax payer in 2022-23 or 2023-24 and received an equal share of distributed luxury-tax proceeds). The Knicks shifting from receiver to payer in FY25 reverses both sides: estimated swing could easily exceed $30-50M of incremental direct operating expense vs. FY24 baseline. The 10-K acknowledges the position but provides no FY25 dollar estimate and no roster-cost guidance.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure exists but is quantitatively soft. This is one of the few cost lines management can semi-control via roster — but FY25 Q3 10-Q already shows player compensation rising and Q3 FY25 net LOSS of $14.2M (vs $37.9M earnings PY) and 9M net loss of $20.7M (vs $33.3M earnings PY). Cost step-up is materializing concurrently with the media-rights cut.

rfm_tuples.R: The Dolan Family Group, by virtue of their stock ownership, have the power to elect all of our directors subject to election by holders of Class B Common Stock and are able collectively to control stockholder decisions... approximately 70.9% of the total voting power of all our outstanding common stock... The Dolan Family Group also controls MSG Entertainment, Sphere Entertainment and AMC Networks Inc.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B insider behavior vs capital events. Pull all Form 4 sales by Dolan family / officers in window leading up to material non-public information about the TSA. The TSA was signed April 24, 2025. Look for sales by insiders in Q1 2025.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Charles F. Dolan 2009 Revocable Trust sold ~36,920 shares for ~$7.0M on March 10-11, 2025 across 12 open-market transactions ($186-$195 range) — Form 4 explicitly does NOT mark these as 10b5-1 plan trades, and the trust is non-officer/non-director ('isOther=true'). Executive Chairman/CEO James L. Dolan sold 15,544 shares for ~$3.1M on March 20, 2025 ($193-$200 range) — also NOT under 10b5-1. Total Dolan-cluster discretionary sales: ~$10M in March 2025, five-six weeks before the April 24 TSA that materially impaired media-rights revenue (28%/18% Knicks/Rangers cuts).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The controlling shareholders unwound stock at $187-$200 in the weeks immediately before disclosing a 25%+ permanent reduction in MSGS's largest contracted revenue stream. Even allowing that a TSA had not yet been signed, the Dolan family sat on both sides of the table (controlling MSGS and controlling Sphere/MSG Networks) and possessed undisclosed information about MSG Networks's pending restructuring concessions. The absence of 10b5-1 protection is the canonical forensic insider-vs-capital-event signal.

rfm_tuples.R: [Critical Audit Matter] Related Party Transactions — Refer to Note 17 to the financial statements... The Dolan family... is the majority beneficial owner of the Company, Sphere Entertainment Co., Madison Square Garden Entertainment Corp., AMC Networks, Inc., and other related entities. In addition, there are overlapping directors and executive officers between the entities.
rfm_tuples.f: Auditor history check. Deloitte & Touche LLP is auditor (Firm ID 34, Big 4, unqualified opinion). Critical Audit Matter is Related Party Transactions — an unusual CAM (typically reserved for areas of material auditor judgment). Run auditor_change_tracker for 5-year lookback.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Auditor: Deloitte & Touche, opinion unqualified, ICFR unqualified. auditor_change_tracker shows 1 Item 4.01 event (2020-11-24) classified as 'resignation/decline' but no Big 4 churn — this was the normal post-Sphere-distribution audit-engagement transition (no disagreements flagged). No auditor change in last 4 years. However, the CAM is unusually thematic: rather than a specific account, the entire related-party complex (revenues $197.6M, arena lease expense $67.6M, services agreement $37.3M, sublease $3.7M, plus 50% AR concentration to MSG Networks) is flagged.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Audit firm is Big 4 with stable tenure — PASS on the structural audit-history dimension. But the auditor's choice to make Related Party Transactions THE Critical Audit Matter is a flag that even Deloitte sees the related-party web as the area of greatest financial-statement misstatement risk. Consistent with the broader Dolan-complex governance opacity.

rfm_tuples.R: As of June 30, 2024, the Company had $184,639 of availability remaining under its stock repurchase authorization. During the year ended June 30, 2024, the Company did not repurchase any shares under its share repurchase program. [Prior year: $75M ASR completed January 31, 2023 at avg $164.31/share]
rfm_tuples.f: Capital action timing. Cross-check whether management was buying back stock when forward visibility was good and stopped when MSG Networks distress became salient — claim_evolution between FY23 and FY24 disclosures.
rfm_tuples.M_value: FY23 (pre-MSG Networks distress acute): $75M ASR executed at $164.31 avg. FY24 (MSG Networks substantial-doubt status emerging at Sphere parent): ZERO buybacks despite $184.6M of remaining authorization, $89M of cash, and stock trading much of the year in the $170-$210 range (similar to ASR price). Note 16 also reveals an $85M ASR (Dec 2021) at $182.69 avg — i.e., the company has aggressively bought when management felt confident but went dark when distress crystallized.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Management capital allocation reads as a tell: stopped buybacks (despite ample authorization and cash) the year before the TSA forced a permanent revenue cut. Sphere's substantial-doubt language predates the MSGS buyback freeze. Read together with C6 (Dolan family insider sales in March 2025), the controlling shareholders chose to monetize personal positions rather than repurchase corporate shares — a structural conflict given the Dolans control both sides of the MSG Networks negotiation.

rfm_tuples.R: Item 3. Legal Proceedings — The Company is a defendant in various lawsuits. Although the outcome of these lawsuits cannot be predicted with certainty (including the extent of available insurance, if any), management does not believe that resolution of these lawsuits will have a material adverse effect on the Company.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B EDGAR full-text counter-check. The legal proceedings disclosure is a single-sentence boilerplate with NO specific case naming. Search EDGAR for material litigation that could plausibly be material (NBA/NHL labor, MSG facial-recognition controversy, Penn Station redevelopment).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Risk factors elsewhere acknowledge Penn Station zoning special permit was renewed Sept 2023 for FIVE years only (vs. prior 10 years), with MTA/NJ Transit/Amtrak having issued a June 2023 'compatibility report' asserting The Garden imposes severe constraints — i.e., there is a known multi-billion-dollar real-estate-relocation overhang that does not appear in Item 3 at all. Also the NYC real-estate tax exemption ($42.2M annual benefit, ~30% of operating income) is under legislative threat per disclosed Jan 2023 elected-official letter and July 2023 NYC IBO report — also absent from Item 3.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Item 3 is technically compliant (no specific litigation rises to material lawsuit standard) but the boilerplate masks material government-action overhangs disclosed elsewhere. A reader who reads only Item 3 would substantially underweight the asset-side risk to The Garden tenancy and tax exemption.

rfm_tuples.R: We Are Controlled by the Dolan Family... James L. Dolan, who has two votes... has the ability to block Dolan Family Committee approval of any Company change in control transaction. The Dolan Family Group also controls MSG Entertainment, Sphere Entertainment and AMC Networks Inc.
rfm_tuples.f: Conflict-of-interest counter-check. The Dolans control both buyer (MSG Sports, paying media-rights fees) and seller (MSG Networks, receiving them) of the local media rights — and now both sides of a Transaction Support Agreement that cuts the rights fees. Test whether the 10-K discloses formation of a special committee or independent process for the TSA.
rfm_tuples.M_value: 10-K (Aug 2024) makes no mention of a Special Committee, independent-director-only review process, or fairness opinion for any prospective MSG Networks restructuring. The 10-K acknowledges Audit Committee approves related-party transactions generically, but disclosure of conflict procedures is by reference to the April 2023 8-K and Exhibit 10.34. The April 24, 2025 8-K disclosing the TSA (filed pre-cutoff) does not appear in this 10-K but in the 10-Q (Note 16 subsequent events) — also no Special Committee disclosure.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: A controlling-shareholder-on-both-sides transaction that permanently cuts ~25% of MSGS's single largest contracted revenue stream was negotiated without any disclosed independent-process protections. Combined with the March 2025 non-10b5-1 insider sales (C6), this is the strongest Mode B finding — a fiduciary process failure adjacent to a related-party transfer of value from MSGS minority shareholders to the Dolan-controlled MSG Networks/Sphere complex.

summary: MSGS 10-K (filed Aug 13, 2024, FY ended June 30, 2024) discloses the structural problem honestly at the risk-factor level — MSG Networks (17% of revenue, 50% of receivables, related-party Sphere subsidiary) was widely understood to be approaching a credit-facility refinancing crisis — but systematically softens the language relative to Sphere Entertainment's own 10-K, which explicitly uses 'substantial doubt about ability to continue as a going concern.' By the May 2, 2025 10-Q (pre-cutoff) MSGS was already booking media-rights revenue at a reduced rate reflecting a Transaction Support Agreement that locks in a 28% Knicks / 18% Rangers permanent rights-fee cut. Q3 FY25 swung to a $14M net loss; 9M to a $20.7M net loss. Two stronger Mode B findings: (1) Charles F. Dolan 2009 Revocable Trust and CEO James L. Dolan made ~$10M of non-10b5-1 discretionary share sales in March 2025 — five to six weeks before the April 24 TSA that they negotiated as the controlling shareholders on both sides; (2) no Special Committee or independent process was disclosed for the conflicted related-party transaction that permanently impaired MSGS's largest contracted revenue stream. Operating fundamentals (Knicks and Rangers brand strength, arena license through 2055) remain intact, but governance behavior in March-April 2025 is a clear forensic red flag.
